name: Twenty
one_liner: Twenty is an open-source, customizable CRM for technical teams, with REST and GraphQL APIs generated per workspace, an app SDK, workflows, AI agents and an MCP server.

auth.note: OAuth2 authorization code + PKCE and client credentials against the API
Bearer API key created in Settings

access.note: Free trial with no credit card; REST & GraphQL API on all plans

api_surface.note: Core and Metadata APIs in REST and GraphQL

mcp.note: Official MCP server at /mcp with OAuth or API key

verdict.note: Documented API with self-serve API keys

notes: API keys are created in Settings, and OAuth clients register dynamically (RFC 7591). The API is generated per workspace schema, so there is no static reference. Rate limit is 50/min on Pro and 100/min on Organization. Webhooks exist. Self-hosting is free. The twenty CLI and twenty-sdk are available.

name: Twilio
one_liner: Twilio is a cloud communications platform offering APIs for SMS, WhatsApp, voice, email (SendGrid), verification, and conversational AI, usable by developers and AI agents.

auth.note: Lists OAuth 2.0, API keys, and Auth Token as supported methods
HTTP Basic auth with API key SID and secret

access.note: Free trial, no credit card required

api_surface.note: REST API at api.twilio.com covering accounts, numbers, calls, messages, usage

mcp.note: Official hosted Twilio MCP server at mcp.twilio.com/docs (public beta, read-only docs search)

verdict.note: Documented auth plus self-serve signup makes it buildable now
Free trial signup with SDKs and curl examples

notes: Official MCP server is public beta and read-only (docs search/retrieve, no credentials, no API execution); execute-capable OAuth MCP tools are only planned. Self-hosted Twilio MCP exists via CLI plugin/Functions. Trial accounts have limits.

name: Plain
one_liner: Plain is a B2B customer support platform that unifies Slack, Teams, email and chat threads, with built-in AI agents, workflows, a GraphQL API and an official MCP server.

auth.note: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE for apps calling the API as a user
Machine user API key for the GraphQL API

access.note: 7-day free trial, no credit card needed
Developer platform (API, Webhooks, MCP) listed in the plans; free trial

api_surface.note: GraphQL API docs with OAuth apps and machine users
MCP sits on top of the GraphQL API

mcp.note: Official MCP server at mcp.plain.com/mcp with nearly 400 tools

verdict.note: Documented API and self-serve OAuth app creation in Settings
Trial available without a credit card

notes: API keys come from machine users (Settings → Machine Users). The MCP server is OAuth-only, which is kept out of auth_methods; OAuth for the GraphQL API is separate. Whether creating OAuth apps or machine users needs an admin role is not shown. Frontier plan lists External Agents. Webhooks exist, but the API is GraphQL.

name: Sherlock
one_liner: Sherlock is an open-source Python command-line tool that checks whether a username exists across 400+ social networks and saves the matches to files.

auth.note: Local CLI run with only a username; no credentials.

access.note: MIT-licensed, installable via pipx or Docker with no signup.

api_surface.note: CLI with JSON, CSV and XLSX output options; no hosted API.

mcp.note: Third-party FastMCP wrapper around the Sherlock CLI; no official MCP found on the official repo page.

verdict.note: A wrappable local CLI counts as buildable_now.

notes: Other fetched pages (Sherlock Labs observability, Sherlock Interview API, Covertlabs sherlock-mcp) are different products and were ignored. No hosted API. The tool probes third-party sites, so site terms and rate limits may apply, and false positives occur.

name: GoHighLevel
one_liner: HighLevel (GoHighLevel) is an all-in-one CRM, marketing automation and agency platform with a v2 REST API, OAuth2 marketplace apps, private integration tokens and an official MCP server.

auth.note: Authorization Code Grant for v2 APIs; client ID/secret from developer app
Private Integration bearer tokens (static OAuth2 access tokens); legacy API keys v1 EOL

access.note: Sign up for a developer account; private apps for internal use, public apps need approval
Paid plans with 14-day free trial; API access listed as core feature

api_surface.note: REST calls to services.leadconnectorhq.com with Bearer token and Version header

mcp.note: Official HighLevel MCP Server docs, 700+ actions
Setup guide with MCP URLs for Claude, Codex, Cursor

verdict.note: Self-generated token from account settings enables direct API use

notes: Private Integrations are created by agency admins; OAuth install needs a location/agency admin. Requires a paid HighLevel plan (14-day trial). Public marketplace apps need approval, but private apps and tokens do not. MCP uses OAuth (separate from API auth). Legacy v1 API keys are end-of-life. Pricing page mentions 'Basic API access' on one tier.

name: Amazon Selling Partner
one_liner: Amazon's Selling Partner API (SP-API) is a REST API that lets sellers and vendors, and developers acting for them, programmatically access orders, listings, inventory, shipments, reports, finances and more.

auth.note: Authorization is based on Login with Amazon (OAuth 2.0)
Authorization workflows and self-authorization for private apps

access.note: Role qualification, architecture review and mandatory Appstore listing for public developers
A seller account/selling plan is also needed

api_surface.note: Many API sections: Orders, Listings, Feeds, Reports, FBA, Vendor and others

mcp.note: Only a beta Selling Partner plugin is mentioned, with no server URL or docs. The Ads MCP Server belongs to Amazon Ads, not SP-API.
No SP-API MCP server listed in the SP-API docs index

verdict.note: The documented REST API requires vendor review of developer registration, roles and the app

notes: Private seller apps can self-authorize, but developer registration and restricted roles still need Amazon approval. Public apps need an architecture review and an Appstore listing. A 'Selling Partner plugin' (beta, for AWS Quick/Claude) is mentioned on a blog with no URL, so it is not counted as MCP. Webhooks exist as Notifications.

name: Datadog
one_liner: Datadog is a cloud observability and security platform for infrastructure, APM, logs, and more, with a REST API and an official MCP server for programmatic and AI-agent access.

auth.note: API key via DD-API-KEY, application key via DD-APPLICATION-KEY
All requests must be authenticated with API and application keys

access.note: Public pricing page; paid plans, keys managed in-account
Keys are managed in your Datadog account

api_surface.note: HTTP REST API with official client libraries in many languages

mcp.note: Official Datadog MCP Server setup docs

verdict.note: Documented REST API with key auth

notes: oauth2 listed because the Datadog docs describe OAuth apps (Application Scope Management) but the fetched pages show OAuth in the MCP context only; the direct API uses API and application keys. The MCP server also accepts API keys. A free trial or signup flow was not directly shown in the fetched pages. The MCP server is unsupported on the ddog-gov sites.

name: Linear
one_liner: Linear is a project and issue tracking tool for software teams, with a GraphQL API, OAuth2 apps, webhooks, a TypeScript SDK and an official hosted MCP server.

auth.note: OAuth2 authorization code, PKCE and client credentials for third-party apps calling the Linear API
Mentions Linear API key / bearer token as an alternative way to authenticate

access.note: The Free plan includes API and webhook access, so credentials are self-serve

api_surface.note: GraphQL API docs, webhooks, attachments, TypeScript SDK and agent docs

mcp.note: Official hosted MCP server at https://mcp.linear.app/mcp
Changelog announcing the official MCP server

verdict.note: API and MCP access are included on every plan, including Free

notes: Personal API keys are inferred from the MCP FAQ mention of a "Linear API key"; the fetched developer pages cover OAuth2 in detail. The OAuth2 docs say each admin user can access an OAuth2 application, and the admin scope is optional. The MCP server uses OAuth 2.1 and also accepts bearer tokens or API keys. Installing an app as actor=app may need workspace admin approval, but the fetched pages do not state this.

name: Devin
one_liner: Devin is Cognition's autonomous AI software engineer that writes, runs and tests code, with a v3 REST API and an official MCP server for managing sessions, playbooks, knowledge and schedules.

auth.note: Service user API keys and PATs, Bearer cog_ tokens; no OAuth2 for third-party apps documented

access.note: Free, Pro $20, Max $200, Teams $80 plans; Devin API listed in plan comparison
Service users provisioned in Settings > Devin API

mcp.note: Official Devin MCP server at mcp.devin.ai with session, playbook, knowledge, and schedule tools

verdict.note: Documented token auth, self-service key provisioning

notes: API access depends on a plan; the pricing comparison table is not clear on which tiers include Devin API, so the access label is inferred. Service user keys are provisioned in org settings, likely by an org admin. The MCP server uses the same API keys, with no OAuth2 for the API. Legacy v1/v2 keys are deprecated.

name: Paygent Connect
one_liner: Paygent is a payment gateway (with a Connect product for platforms and marketplaces, plus Payouts, Subscriptions and Tapn tap-to-pay) that offers REST APIs, SDKs and webhooks.

auth.note: Sample request uses a Bearer API key (pgt_live_xxx)

access.note: Free plan, no credit card required

api_surface.note: REST APIs, SDKs, webhooks and sandbox are advertised
Docs page mentions the Pathfinder API, Collect.js and Three-Step Redirect

mcp.note: No MCP server found on the fetched official pages

verdict.note: Self-serve signup and a documented REST API suggest it is buildable

notes: The docs page is thin. The homepage shows Bearer-key auth against api.paygent.com, while the docs page mentions the NMI-style Pathfinder API, Collect.js and Three-Step Redirect, so the two may differ. The GitLab pages are a different (Japanese Paygent) module and were not used. Endpoint details and auth are not confirmed in full docs.
